key_insight: Classical–quantum fusion can improve prediction when its representations capture complementary relationships, but matched classical representations can provide the same benefit.
clinical_relevance: Breast cancer diagnostic benchmarking suggests relevance to biomedical prediction, but the abstract does not establish cancer drug discovery utility or clinical benefit.
method: Preserve full classical inputs alongside simulated quantum features.
Combine representations using concatenation or attention.
Assess contributions using single-view, replacement and masking controls.
evidence_signal: Controlled experiments and benchmark evaluations showed improved mean performance over classical baselines on four datasets, including Wisconsin Diagnostic Breast Cancer, while classical baselines led on Digits and Covertype.
watch_item: Gains depend on representation–target alignment and fusion strategy; competitive classical controls mean the findings do not establish a uniquely quantum advantage.
paper_title: When do quantum views help? Complementary classical-quantum representations in multi-view fusion
